crosswalks.label: Software Developers
crosswalks.rationale: Software Developers cover implementation and hardware/software integration relevant to firmware/device software but do not isolate embedded target, revision or physical-evidence boundaries.

crosswalks.label: Computer Hardware Engineers
crosswalks.rationale: Computer Hardware Engineers explicitly evaluate hardware/software interfaces and physical hardware design/test, supplying the adjacent ownership boundary rather than an embedded-software identity.

findings.summary: O*NET software and hardware occupational evidence jointly grounds the hardware/software interface work around embedded software while showing that the work crosses two profession families rather than one exact occupation.
method_labels: O*NET 31.0 Software Developer and Computer Hardware Engineer occupation/task baselines
findings.rationale: The candidate body narrows the overlap into firmware, target constraints, hardware-interface implementation and recovery while preserving physical/hardware ownership.

findings.summary: Simulation, target execution, document applicability and physical observation are distinct evidence surfaces; software machinery must not infer physical or safety behavior from simulator-only proof.
findings.rationale: Hardware/software occupational overlap makes the evidence boundary a first-class contract for a reusable embedded package.

gaps_against_body.description: Make simulator/target/document/physical-observation evidence surfaces explicit and require hardware/safety ownership for claims that cross software-only observability.

nonclaims: This packet does not claim complete reconstruction of Embedded Software Engineer.
Software Developer and Computer Hardware Engineer mappings remain partial/adjacent rather than AXM profession identity.
No physical-device correctness, electrical, safety, manufacturing, TEST, WORKING or CANON claim is created by this research packet.

high_stakes.authorization_nonclaim: This packet grants no hardware, electrical, safety, manufacturing, physical-device deployment or institutional authority.
